paper.title: StandardE2E: A Unified Framework for End-to-End Autonomous Driving Datasets

review.question: 近一年空间数据的生产难点在哪里，具身机器人与智能驾驶的异同是什么？

relevance.reason: The paper directly identifies schema, coordinate, calibration and modality fragmentation as a recurring production and reuse cost for driving datasets.

sections_read.purpose: Map cross-dataset fragmentation and its engineering cost.

sections_read.locator: 3 The StandardE2E framework; 3.1 The adapter chain
sections_read.purpose: Inspect the canonical schema and transformation boundary.

sections_read.locator: 3.2 Segment-context aggregators; 3.3 Indexing and scenario filtering; 3.4 The UnifiedE2EDataset
sections_read.purpose: Assess the supported operations and handling of missing modalities and temporal context.

sections_skipped.reason: not-applicable: the paper is an extended abstract and states that the full cross-dataset analysis is still in preparation.

research_question: Can a canonical schema and adapter chain reduce the repeated engineering cost of turning heterogeneous driving logs into training-ready spatial data?
contributions: Defines a canonical per-frame schema spanning cameras, LiDAR, maps, detections, ego state and trajectories.
Separates one-time deterministic preprocessing from training-time loading, filtering and multi-dataset mixing.

method.summary: Maps each native dataset into StandardFrameData, applies configurable modality adapters and segment-context aggregators, writes deterministic frame caches and a scenario index, then exposes them through a unified PyTorch dataset.
assumptions: Every source dataset can be mapped to the canonical semantics without unacceptable information loss
Missing modalities can be explicitly flagged and default-filled

embodiments: Autonomous-driving datasets with heterogeneous sensor rigs
study_context.sample_or_scale: Six supported datasets in the released framework; full empirical cross-dataset analysis not yet reported.

evaluation.design: System description and fixture-level reproducibility checks rather than a comparative scientific experiment.
baselines: Native per-dataset APIs and project-specific preprocessing
metrics: Deterministic cache equivalence via unit tests

findings.finding: Dataset heterogeneity extends beyond file formats to calibration conventions, coordinate systems and missing modality coverage, making cross-dataset reuse expensive and brittle.
findings.scope: The six driving datasets supported by the framework and the broader ecosystem described by the paper.

findings.finding: Canonicalization improves reuse only by making per-dataset mappings explicit; it does not make absent modalities or semantic mismatches disappear.

author_stated.limitation: The document is an extended abstract and the full cross-dataset analyses are still in preparation.

reader_inferred.boundary: The work demonstrates interface unification, not that coordinate or label semantics are scientifically equivalent across datasets.
reader_inferred.basis: Missing modalities are default-filled and each dataset still requires a hand-written raw-to-canonical mapping.

transfer_boundary: Useful for reducing integration toil when source semantics are understood; insufficient as evidence that heterogeneous datasets can be mixed without distribution shift or supervision mismatch.

design_strengths: Makes coordinate, modality and temporal-context handling explicit
design_risks: Canonical schemas may hide source-specific uncertainty or semantics
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: No controlled baseline comparison is reported in the extended abstract.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Engineering support and determinism measure integration quality, not learning benefit or safety.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: The package, schemas and unit-test approach are described and publicly linked.
critical_appraisal.external_validity: Applies to supported driving datasets; extension cost and semantic loss for new sensor types remain unquantified.

evidence_cards.claim: Driving-data fragmentation is itself a production bottleneck: dataset-specific file formats, APIs, calibration conventions and modality coverage make preprocessing repeatedly reimplemented and cross-dataset experiments expensive and brittle.
evidence_cards.relation: Limits the assumption that once raw spatial data are collected, they are naturally reusable across driving datasets or models.
evidence_cards.summary: The introduction explicitly describes recurring per-project preprocessing and brittle adapter work caused by heterogeneous dataset conventions.
evidence_cards.source_context: In practice, this fragmentation imposes a recurring tax on end-to-end driving research. Per project, researchers re-implement preprocessing pipelines from raw protobuf, parquet, pickled-frame, or city-wide GPKG sources into a representation their model can consume.

verification.rationale: The claim closely paraphrases the exact problem statement and does not assert unreported model improvements.
